documents.title: Bambu Lab R1 Spec Sheet
documents.note: Two pages headed "Bambu Lab R1 Spec sheet" (printed page numbers 14 and 15). The store "R1 Specs" block links it as a "Download PDF" button (downloadButton.downloadUrl); the package collects no document from this page, so this curated entry is its only document row.

documents.title: Packing List for the Bambu Lab R1

notes: Registry gap, not a data gap: the registry has no laser-machine keys, so these published rows of the sheet (and the store table) are neither specs nor not_published: Max cutting capacity per lens (15 / 18 / 18 mm black walnut, 20 mm acrylic), Spot size per lens (Ø0.11 / 0.17 / 0.19 mm), Absolute motion accuracy with Vision Encoder (<0.1 mm @600 mm), Air assist pump (30 L/min @30 kPa), Positioning system and accuracy (<0.2 mm), Panoramic capture, Detail capture, Focusing, Toolhead positioning measure, Curved surface / Cylinder / Revolve shape processing, Laser alignment, One-tap setup, Autofocus, Automatic material recognition, System health management, Safety interlocks, Safety key, Emergency stop, Wi-Fi TX power; and from the store page only: Max. material size (710 × 380 mm standalone; up to 610 mm wide with the Conveyor), wavelength 9–11 µm and processing height 0–58 mm (up to 248 mm with the height-increasing base) from FAQ 3.

Supported materials: the sheet's "Supported materials" row is recorded as compatible_with relations (target_kind material, one per material, condition "Cut and engrave" or "Engrave only"); the store "Full material list" adds stone & slate (engrave only) as compatible_with, and bare metal and PVC / chlorine-containing materials as not_compatible_with.

Store notes that qualify those rows (kept for when keys exist): wood means plywood; the medium- and long-focus capacities need lenses sold separately (footnote 1); automatic material recognition only for Bambu Lab official materials (table footnote 2); at launch only Cylinder Processing is supported, Revolve Shape Processing comes in a later firmware (page footnote 4); the Vision Encoder is sold separately (footnote 5).

Left out on purpose (neither a spec nor not_published), because they do not fit a laser cutter: printing.build_volume (the sheet gives a 2-D working area, recorded as printing.working_area), printing.layer_height, printing.build_plate, printing.supported_filament / unsupported_filament, the filament sensors and odometry, printing.auto_leveling (the R1 has autofocus, not bed levelling), printing.multi_color, motion.max_flow, extrusion.*, thermal.*, electrical.battery / connector / requirements / steady_state_power. Also left out: printing.camera (the sheet names a "Dual-camera" positioning system and the page a "Toolhead Camera", but no monitoring camera row), carton.*, compat.statement, identity.*, package.volume_m3, manufacturer_terms.*, variant.note.

Region: every electrical and package row is region-free (region ""). The sheet is the single global table (FCC/CE/SRRC) and gives a universal 100–240 VAC input; the US store table is identical, so it is not a 100–120 V US table; the messages bundle has no R1 values. No us_110v or intl_220v row exists for this product.

Consistency with the parsed store page: the package gives 0 spec rows for this page, so mergeCurated meets no overlap. Every sheet value was also compared by hand with the store "R1 Specs" table: all agree (the store table adds footnote markers, footnotes 1–4 and one extra row, "Max. material size the machine can accommodate").

Marketing numbers not recorded: "nearly 3× as fast" (page footnote 2), "about a third less space" (footnote 8), "in just one minute" alignment, "Draw 300 mm. Cut 300 mm.", "up to 18 mm walnut and 20 mm acrylic" (the sheet's table values cover it).
Not recorded: per-version availability, and the store's SEO meta line (commercial and returns terms, not specifications).
